items.title: The bivariant group of a morphism between disjoint unions is the product of the bivariant groups of its pieces
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the bivariant group of a morphism of disjoint union decompositions as the product of the bivariant groups of the pieces, over an arbitrary index set (statement lines 6622-6634, tag 0FDZ). The proof builds both maps explicitly and then has to check the non-trivial composite: for a fixed piece of the target it uses that a bivariant class commutes with flat pullback to move the restriction of the cap into the pullback, and that it commutes with proper pushforward to identify the pushed forward restricted cap with the cap of the pushed forward class. Because the indices are arbitrary, the argument has to be phrased through the product decompositions of the Chow groups rather than finitely many cases, which is the substance, so the claim is H2.
